Thought: To determine the point group of the molecule with the given SMILES "CS(=O)C", I need to first understand the molecular structure it represents. The SMILES notation "CS(=O)C" describes a molecule with a sulfur atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom (sulfoxide) and bonded to two methyl groups (CH3). The central sulfur atom makes the molecule potentially asymmetric. The point group of this molecule can be deduced based on its symmetry elements.

The steps to identify the point group are:

1. Check for rotational axes (Cn). The molecule could have a C2 axis if there is symmetry around the S=O bond.
2. Check for mirror planes (σ). The molecule could have a mirror plane if the two methyl groups are equivalent.
3. Check for inversion centers (i) and improper axes (Sn).

Given the structure of dimethyl sulfoxide, the molecule has a mirror plane but no rotational axis or center of inversion, which indicates its point group is Cs.
